transcript.speaker: Clarity
transcript.dialogue: Craig Reynolds's 1987 paper asks how a flock can move together without giving every bird a scripted path  Begin with separation.

transcript.speaker: Clarity
transcript.dialogue: Alignment matches the average velocity of nearby agents  It gradually coordinates their headings.

transcript.speaker: Clarity
transcript.dialogue: Cohesion steers an agent toward the local center of its neighbors  It is different from alignment: location and heading are different information.

transcript.speaker: Clarity
transcript.dialogue: Select follow one agent  Its halo marks the distance limit, while the links identify neighbors within the forward-biased field of view.

transcript.speaker: Clarity
transcript.dialogue: The group pattern emerges from repeated local decisions  No agent sees the whole flock and no leader assigns its route.

transcript.speaker: Clarity
transcript.dialogue: Finally, keep the limits visible  This example uses a small three-dimensional flock, weighted steering, a fixed time step and wrapping boundaries.
